definition: A system design in which ongoing human feedback (ratings, corrections, preferences) is continually collected and used to improve a deployed AI system over time.
details: Human feedback loops are used both during model training (as in RLHF) and in production systems, where user interactions and corrections can inform future model updates or fine-tuning.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Human Feedback Loop — is what makes everything else possible.
